title: Structured Output & Tool/Function Calling: Acceptance Criteria and Error/Streaming Modes
creator: Lina Chen
description: Problem statement: Customers using Redwood’s chat and tool-calling features need deterministic, machine-parseable outputs for downstream automation (e.g., agent orchestration, 3rd-party tools). Current model outputs are semi-structured and exhibit multiple failure modes: schema divergence, truncated streaming events, ambiguous function invocations, and inconsistent error signaling. This ticket defines acceptance criteria and implementation constraints for structured output plus function/tool calling behaviors across sync and streaming modes. Goal: have a clear contract for schemas, well-defined error modes, and deterministic streaming chunks so SDKs and customers can reliably parse and recover from failures.
background: Referenced artifacts: design notes in Confluence (doc link placeholder), prototype SDK PR #142 on GitHub, and an internal eval run that found 12% schema-mismatch rate on typical SQL-generation prompts. This work aligns with the Structured Output initiative and API-2026.04 release. Stakeholders: API PM, Runtime team, SDKs, Console team, Customer-facing Solutions.
scope: In-scope: acceptance criteria for JSON/YAML/typed outputs, function/tool calling contract (name, arguments schema, deterministic invocation), streaming event envelope formats, explicit error classes and recovery semantics, SDK parsing helpers and conformance tests. Out-of-scope: model fine-tuning to improve correctness; downstream orchestration orchestration policy engines (only provide observability hooks).
requirements_clarification: 1) Supported schema formats: JSON Schema draft-07 or later for object schemas; a small typed YAML shorthand allowed for readability but must map to JSON Schema. 2) Function/tool signature registration: server accepts a published signature for each function with an id, name, and JSON Schema for args. 3) Models MUST emit a top-level deterministic wrapper when function calling is used (see schema_spec). 4) Streaming must guarantee chunk ordering and reassembly semantics; each chunk has a stable 'chunk_id' and 'stream_pos'. 5) When schema validation fails, models/runtime must emit an explicit error envelope rather than free-form text. 6) SDKs will expose both strict and permissive parsers; acceptance criteria apply to strict mode. Any clarification requests will be tracked in sub-issues.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Schema conformance: For 100 representative prompts in our acceptance test suite, generated outputs accepted by the registered JSON Schema validator in strict mode for >= 98% of cases. 2) Function invocation deterministic mapping: when model signals a function call, the server must emit a single invocation event with fields: function_id, name, args (object), confidence_score (optional numeric string). No ambiguous multiple-function outputs allowed in strict mode. 3) Error envelopes: three canonical error kinds must be produced by the runtime when problems occur: 'schema_mismatch', 'partial_stream', 'function_resolution_error'. Each error envelope must include 'error_code', 'message', 'original_text' (if available), and 'recovery_suggestion'. 4) Streaming semantics: chunked outputs must include sequence metadata (chunk_id, stream_pos, is_last). Reassembly by SDK must result in byte-identical payload to a non-streamed output when no partial errors occur. 5) Partial outputs: if the model truncates mid-JSON, the runtime must deliver a 'partial_stream' error with the last valid parse offset and allow SDK to request a 'resume' which triggers model to emit only the missing suffix. 6) Backwards-compatibility: legacy clients (per protocol flag) still receive previous freeform text events bundled under 'legacy_text' but default API returns structured envelopes. 7) Tests: automated tests for validators, streaming reassembly, and error envelope handling must exist and pass in CI. 8) Documentation: update API spec, SDK guides, and Console schema viewer before release.
error_modes:
Define three standard error classes emitted as structured envelopes:
1) schema_mismatch - emitted when final reconstructed payload fails JSON Schema validation. Fields: error_code='schema_mismatch', severity=('warning'|'error'), failed_schema_path, original_payload_snippet. Recovery: either 'auto-correct' attempt (non-default) or provide explicit 'fixup_suggestions' array.
2) partial_stream - emitted when stream closes unexpectedly or model truncates output. Fields: error_code='partial_stream', last_valid_offset, stream_id, resume_token (if available). Recovery: SDK may call the /streams/:id/resume endpoint with resume_token.
3) function_resolution_error - emitted when declared function_id/name cannot be mapped to a registered tool at runtime. Fields: error_code='function_resolution_error', declared_function_id, available_candidates (array up to 5), fallback_strategy ('drop'|'emit_legacy_text'|'noop').
Errors must be logged to the Console with linkable event IDs.
streaming_behavior: Streaming envelope must be newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) with each chunk shaped as: {"stream_id":string, "chunk_id":int, "stream_pos":int, "is_last":bool, "payload_type":('content'|'error'|'meta'), "payload":string-or-object}. Guarantee: chunk ordering preserved by runtime; if out-of-order delivery detected, SDK throws a reassembly error. Chunks for function args may be large; chunking must split on UTF-8 codepoint boundaries and not slice inside multi-byte characters. For streaming function calls, the function_call envelope MUST appear as a single logical object once reassembled; partial/early function signals allowed but must follow the partial_stream error semantics. SDKs: offer automatic reassembly with heuristics for flow-control and an opt-in manual streaming API.
function_call_contracts: Registration: publishers register tool signatures via /register_tool with payload {id, name, description, json_schema}. The runtime stores a canonical mapping and exposes it to models. Invocation flow: 1) Model emits function_call envelope. 2) Runtime validates function_id vs registry. 3) If valid, runtime emits a function_invocation event to downstream tool worker; if invalid, emit function_resolution_error. Arguments: args must be a JSON object strictly conforming to provided schema when operating in strict mode. If args exceed size limit (configurable per account), runtime emits function_resolution_error with fallback_strategy='emit_legacy_text'. Concurrency: a single chat session can have up to 4 concurrent in-flight function invocations; additional requests are queued.
edge_cases: 1) Ambiguous multiple-function outputs: if model lists multiple candidate functions, strict mode rejects (emit function_resolution_error) and suggests top-1; permissive mode picks top-1 by highest model score. 2) Binary blobs in args: not supported in structured args; encode as base64 and schema must declare 'content_encoding': 'base64'. 3) Schema with circular refs: allowed only if resolvable via $id and /schemas endpoint. 4) Very large args (>1MB): trigger error_code='args_too_large' and recommend chunked payload via signed upload link.
test_plan: QA checklist and automated tests to be committed to the repo: 1) Schema conformance suite: 100 positive/negative cases per registered function. 2) Streaming reassembly fuzzing: randomized chunk boundaries, out-of-order delivery injected; ensure SDK reassembly passes for valid sequences and raises for corrupted streams. 3) Error envelope handling: simulate schema_mismatch, partial_stream, function_resolution_error and validate SDK and Console events. 4) End-to-end integration: register sample tool, drive prompts to trigger function_call, validate invocation arrives at worker with args intact, and validate logs/trace ids are present. 5) Backwards-compatibility test: legacy client flag returns legacy_text payload and old parsers still function. 6) Load test: 1k concurrent streaming sessions with mixed function calls to verify resource limits and queueing.
rollout_plan: Phased rollout across environments: 1) Canary (internal customers + staging): enable strict structured_output by default for 5 internal customers for 2 weeks. 2) Beta: opt-in for existing customers via API flag for 4 weeks; collect telemetry and fixup suggestions. 3) General availability: default strict structured_output on for new accounts; existing accounts can opt-in via console toggle for 30 days before opt-out window closes. Communication: update changelog, send targeted emails to power users, and add Console banner. If error rates >1% on schema_mismatch during Beta, halt rollout and revert defaults.
monitoring_and_metrics: Expose the following metrics to Console and alerts: structured_output.schema_mismatch.count, structured_output.partial_stream.count, function_resolution_error.count, streaming.reassembly.latency.p95, function_invocation.latency.p95, function_invocation.failure_rate. Also track customer-impacting errors and surface top 10 failing schemas in Console. Set alert thresholds: schema_mismatch.rate > 0.5% over 1h for GA accounts => Pager.
notes: Follow-up: create a small 'schema discovery' UI in Console to preview registered schemas and test example payloads. Create a separate ENG ticket for resume-token auth and secure upload links. Track customer feedback via feature-flag telemetry and add opt-out hooks for accounts with custom tooling that cannot adapt.
